run.procedureSummary: 1 Charge: add the cycle's charge row to positions 1-6; no cap at this step. 2 Overflow: go through positions 1 to 6 in order. Anything above working volume goes into the next crucible, leaving this one exactly at volume. Overflow from 6 goes to slag. Upstream overflow is added before the next crucible is checked, so it can cascade. 3 State check, on the melt after overflow: BASE at or above the upper mark becomes SUPERHEATED; SUPERHEATED at or below the lower mark becomes BASE. Each crucible is checked once per cycle, so it changes at most once. 4 Draw-down: work out all six amounts from the melt after overflow first. BASE sends floor(q/4) to slag. SUPERHEATED sends floor(q/2) to position i-1, and position 1's goes to slag. All six moves happen at the same time, and a crucible can be left over volume. 5 Emergency tap: if the line total is strictly over 38, each crucible keeps floor(q/2) and the rest goes to slag. At 38 or under, nothing happens.

openPoints.point: Which melt the draw-down amounts are taken from
openPoints.assumption: The melt after overflow, which is also the melt the state check used. The states used are the ones just set by this cycle's state check.

openPoints.point: Return melt that leaves a crucible over volume
openPoints.assumption: It stays there and nothing is checked again within the cycle. The next cycle's overflow step clears it. After cycle 5 it stays over (crucible 2 ends at 10 against a volume of 8).
Each crucible keeps floor(q/2) and gives up ceil(q/2) to slag.
The tap fires only when the total is strictly over 38. In cycle 5 the total is exactly 38, so it does not fire.
Both marks count as reached when melt equals them: BASE changes at melt >= upper, and SUPERHEATED changes back at melt <= lower.

openPoints.point: Whether the emergency tap changes states
openPoints.assumption: It does not. States change only in step 3.

run.notes: I did the arithmetic with a short Python script, piped in through stdin, and checked cycle 1 by hand. The shared scratchpad's sim.py was overwritten by another process while I was working: its content was different, used the state word "LARVAL", and gave one stray run. I disregarded that file and its output. The figures above come only from my own stdin run. Crucible 2 ends at 10, over its working volume of 8, because of return melt in the cycle 5 draw-down. The write-up allows this.
